description: The plot illustrates how classification accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale with major ticks shown at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³; the plotted points appear at four increasing co-occurrence values spanning from roughly 5 to roughly 3000. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)”, uses a linear scale, and ranges from 60 to 85 with tick marks every 5 percentage points. The Base line is black with circular markers and a solid line, increasing from about 64% at the smallest co-occurrence value to about 71% at the largest, with intermediate points near 66.5% and 69%. The FT line is blue with downward-triangle markers and a solid line, rising from about 65% to about 73%, passing through roughly 69% and 71.5%. The IKE line is red with upward-triangle markers and a solid line, increasing from about 67.5% to about 75.2%, with middle values around 71.8% and 74.2%. The MEND line is brown with diamond markers and a solid line, increasing from about 70.7% to about 80.1%, with intermediate points near 75.6% and 78.5%. The MEMIT line is purple with pentagon markers and a solid line, rising from about 69.5% to about 77.6%, with intermediate values around 73.8% and 76.9%. The ROME line is green with square markers and a solid line, increasing from about 74.3% to about 84.2%, with intermediate points near 79.5% and 82.3%.
